subject: Staggered rollout concession request for MerchantCo activation
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Product Team <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Eng Lead <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, CS Ops <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-03-12T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: MerchantCo - ask: staggered rollout / concession to close Q2

Team,

Quick context: MerchantCo is our top mid-market closure this quarter — $750k ARR first-year committed, procurement wants activation in 6 weeks. Legal/procurement have signed off contingent on a controlled rollout promise: they need a bounded activation plan that limits exposure for the first 10k monthly active users and a clear rollback plan.

Their deal desk has pushed hard for a production-level tenant isolation guarantee (which would be a product-facing workstream). To unblock the contract in time, I want to propose a concession: a staggered rollout where we (a) enable the integration for a limited subset of traffic and (b) operate under explicit canary SLOs rather than full tenant isolation at launch.

Attachments: MerchantCo_MAP.pdf (mutual action plan) and SOW_v0.3.docx (procurement draft).

Ask: can Product/Eng sign up to a 4-week canary + automated rollback criteria and commit to a follow-up full isolation milestone within 10 weeks? If we can get a short written commitment, procurement will proceed with signatures.

I appreciate trade-offs here — happy to join a technical sync. Proposed times: Thu 3/12 3pm PT or Fri 3/13 10am PT.

— Karthik
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Eng Lead <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: CS Ops <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-12T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MerchantCo - ask: staggered rollout / concession to close Q2

Karthik — thanks for the heads up and the MAP. I skimmed the SOW and have a few clarifying questions before we commit to any timeline:

1) What is the expected QPS / token-per-request profile for the initial 10k MAU canary? MerchantCo gave a broad range in the deck; we need a target percentile to size autoscaling and warm pools.
2) Are they requiring deterministic trace retention or any export hooks for compliance during the canary window? That will affect storage and observability work.
3) Does MerchantCo expect a tenant-level kill-switch (we can offer a route-level throttle as an interim step), and what are their rollback acceptance criteria?

From a product perspective, a 4-week canary with documented pass/fail gates is reasonable if we limit scope to configuration + routing policies and avoid structural isolation (multi-tenant network carveouts) in that window. However, engineering ETA depends on the answers above and on whether we need additional telemetry events instrumented.

I can attend Thu 3/12 3pm PT. Please include any traffic/cost projections in advance.

— Marissa
Director, Product Management
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-03-12T12:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MerchantCo - ask: staggered rollout / concession to close Q2

Adding a few customer-facing constraints from CS:

- MerchantCo's legal team has made clear the deal approval timeline is tight — they have a board meeting on 2026-03-19 and need signatures before then.
- They are OK with a canary if: (1) we provide a written canary runbook, (2) there is a one-click rollback plan, and (3) we agree to a post-canary remediation/roadmap item for full isolation.
- Success criteria they care about: <1% error rate on payment-related endpoints, latency P95 < 450ms for the canary cohort, and no PII leakage in telemetry exports.

We can own the runbook and validation scripts from the customer side, but we need Product/Eng sign-off on rollback instrumentation and on storage/export settings. If Product can commit to a 4-week canary and a 10-week isolation milestone with milestones in the MAP, procurement will sign.

Happy to run the customer call and walk through the canary acceptance gates.

— Monica
Senior Customer Success Manager
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Park <samantha@merchantco.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@merchantco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-13T08:09:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MerchantCo - ask: staggered rollout / concession to close Q2

Samantha / Tom — thanks again for the call. Per our discussion, we put the MAP and SOW in the attachments. Summary of the plan we discussed:

- Phase 1 (canary): enable integration for a capped cohort (10k MAU cap), 4-week run, rollback criteria in runbook.
- Phase 2 (remediation): Product/Eng to deliver full tenant isolation as a milestone within 10 weeks of canary start.
- Procurement: MerchantCo will start signature process once Product provides a one-paragraph written commitment to the above timing.

Marissa / Jordan / Monica — I need a quick one-paragraph commitment that I can share with MerchantCo legal by EOD tomorrow (3/13) to keep their board timeline. If engineering needs scope reductions to hit the dates, please call it out.

DocuSign note: Tom, I sent a provisional envelope to your team — we'll replace the date with the final commitment text once we have it.

— Karthik
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-03-15T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MerchantCo - ask: staggered rollout / concession to close Q2

Karthik / team — after an internal scoping session with Eng, here is what we can commit to and the caveats: 

Commitment (one-paragraph for procurement): Redwood will support a controlled 4-week canary for MerchantCo capped at the agreed cohort size, with automated rollback triggers, documented runbook, and post-canary remediation work to deliver full tenant isolation within 10 weeks from canary start.

Caveats & required inputs: 
- We need MerchantCo to confirm target QPS and token profile (or sign off on our default estimate of 120 reqs/min during peak) by 2026-03-17.
- Engineering will ship a route-level throttle/kill-switch for the canary; full network-level isolation requires the separate roadmap item (tracked in SUP-2241) and additional infra capacity (estimated 3 sprint points + one on-call engineer for rollout week).
- If telemetry export toggles are required for compliance, we need a sign-off on retention limits and access controls; otherwise we'll keep exports disabled for the canary.

If MerchantCo accepts the above constraints and signs the MAP/SOW this week, we will prepare the canary runbook and target the canary start for 2026-03-23.

— Jordan
Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference
